Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 75, verses 5–7:

﴿Nay, but man wishes to continue in sin before him﴾. He says: the son of Adam does not fail to know that his Lord is able to gather his bones, but he wishes to continue in sin before him, that is, he proceeds forward [in] [[In "B": "fi" (in).]] the disobediences of God as long as he lives, riding his head (i.e., headlong), not turning back from them and not repenting. This is the saying of Mujahid, al-Hasan, Ikrimah, and al-Suddi.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "to continue in sin before him" means he advances into sin and delays repentance, saying: "I will repent, I will act later," until death comes to him in the worst of his states and his most evil deeds [[See: Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra': 3/208.]].

Al-Dahhak said: it is hope (al-amal), he says: "I will live and obtain such-and-such from the world," [and does not remember death] [[What is between the brackets is omitted from "B".]].

Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd said: he denies what lies before him of the Resurrection and the Reckoning. The root of "fujur" (depravity, transgression) is inclination (al-mayl), and the wicked person and the disbeliever are called "fajir" (depraved) because of their inclination away from the truth.

﴿He asks: when is the Day of Resurrection?﴾, that is, when will it occur, [mocking] and denying it. God Most High said: ﴿So when the sight is dazzled﴾. The people of Madina read "baraqa" with a fatha on the ra', and the others read it with a kasra, and both are dialects.

Qatadah and Muqatil said: the sight becomes fixed and does not blink at what it sees of the marvels which it used to deny in the world. It is said: this occurs at death.

Al-Kalbi said: at the sight of Hell the eyes of the disbelievers are dazzled.

Al-Farra' and al-Khalil said: "bariqa" with a kasra means he was terrified and bewildered by what he sees of the marvels. And "baraqa" with a fatha means he split his eye and opened it wide, from al-buruq, which is glittering (al-talalu'). [[Ibn Jarir said (29/179): "The more correct of the two readings in our view is the kasra in (fa-idha bariqa), meaning: he was terrified, so he split and opened (his eyes) from the terror of the Resurrection and the fear of death, and this is how Arab poetry has come. Some narrators recited to me from Abu Ubaydah al-Kilabi: 'When Ibn Subayh came to me, desiring, I gave him a she-camel of 'Isa, from which he was dazzled (fa-baraqa).'"]]

There is no refuge]: no fortress, no shelter, and no place of safety. Al-Suddi said: "There is no mountain." When they were frightened, they used to flee to the mountain and fortify themselves in it. [God the Exalted said] [[In manuscript "B": "fa-qala", "Say".]] "There is no mountain that will protect them on that Day."

ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud said: it means the destination and the return. Its parallel is God the Exalted's saying: "To your Lord is the return" [al-ʿAlaq: 8], and "To God is the final destination" [Āl ʿImrān: 28; al-Nūr: 42; Fāṭir: 18].

Mujahid said: his first deed and his last deed. ʿAṭāʾ said: what he put forward in the first part of his life, and what he left behind in the last part of his life.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 75, verse 14–16:

﴿Nay, man will be a witness against himself﴾. ʿIkrimah, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: its meaning is: "Nay, man is a witness against himself from himself. There are watchers (ruqaba') who observe him and bear witness against him by his deeds, and they are his hearing, his sight and his limbs" [[See: Maʿani al-Quran by al-Farra': 3/211.]]. The ha' (feminine marker) entered into baṣīrah because the intended meaning of "man" here is his limbs. It is also possible that its meaning is "Nay, man is a witness against himself," meaning: to his limbs, so the preposition was omitted, as in His saying: ﴿And if you wish to seek wet-nurses for your children﴾ [al-Baqarah: 233], i.e., for your children. It is also permissible that it be an adjective for a feminine noun, i.e., "Nay, man against himself is a seeing eye" (ʿayn baṣīrah).

Abu al-ʿAliyah and ʿAta' said: "Nay, man against himself is a witness," and this is the narration of al-ʿAwfi from Ibn ʿAbbas. The ha' in baṣīrah is for emphasis (mubalaghah), and the proof of this interpretation is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Sufficient is your own self against you this day as a reckoner﴾ [al-Isra': 14].

﴿Though he were to offer his excuses﴾: meaning, a witness will testify against him, and even if he made excuses and argued on behalf of himself, it would not benefit him, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿On the day when their excuses will not benefit the wrongdoers﴾ [Ghafir: 52]. This is the view of Mujahid, Qatadah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ibn Zayd and ʿAta'. Al-Farra' said: "Even if he makes excuses, there is against him from his own self one who will refute his excuse." The meaning of "ilqa'" (casting) here is "saying," as in His saying: ﴿And they will say to them, "You are indeed liars"﴾ [al-Nahl: 86]. Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: "Though he were to offer his excuses" means: even if he let down the curtains and closed the doors. The people of Yemen call a curtain "mi'dhar," and its plural is "ma'adhir," and the meaning according to this view is: even if he lowers the curtain to hide what he does, his own self is a witness against him. The saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it﴾

We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi, who said: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, who said: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, who said: Jarir narrated to us, from Musa ibn Abi ʿAʾishah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, regarding His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: "Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it." He said: When Jibril came down to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with the revelation, he would often move his tongue and lips, and this was difficult for him, and it was noticed in him. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed the verse found in "Nay, I swear by the Day of Resurrection": ﴿Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it﴾ [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, Tafsir Surat al-Qiyamah, chapter "Indeed upon Us is its collection and its recitation": 8/682, and Muslim in Salah, chapter on listening to the recitation, no. (448): 1/330.]]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 75, verses 24–28:**

﴿And faces that Day will be gloomy﴾: frowning, scowling, dusty, blackened.

Ibn Zayd said: "It is entering the Fire." Al-Kalbi said: "It is being veiled from seeing the Lord, Mighty and Majestic."

Qatadah said: "They sought physicians for him, but they could not avail him anything against the decree of Allah."

Sulayman al-Taymi and Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: this is the speech of the angels, some of them saying to others: "Who will ascend with his soul?" Then the angels of mercy or the angels of punishment ascend with it.

﴿And he thinks﴾: those whose souls have reached the collarbones are certain ﴿that it is the parting﴾ from the world.

**Al-Baghawi's commentary (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on Surah 75, verses 36–40:**

﴿Does man suppose that he will be left neglected (sudan)?﴾ *Sudan* means left aimless, unordered and unforbidden. Al-Suddi said: its meaning is "neglected." It is said of camels: *ibil sudan*, when they graze wherever they wish without a herdsman.

﴿Was he not a drop of semen emitted (yumna)?﴾ That is, poured into the womb. Hafs, from Asim, read *yumna* with a *ya'* (*yumana*). This is also the reading of al-Hasan. The others read it with a *ta'* (*tumna*), referring to the *nutfah* (drop).

﴿Then he became a clinging clot, and He created and proportioned (fasawwa)﴾: He put the spirit into him and perfected his form.

﴿And made of him two sexes, the male and the female﴾: He created from his water offspring, males and females.

﴿Is not that One﴾ who did this ﴿able to give life to the dead?﴾

Abu Tahir Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Qashani informed us: Abu Amr al-Qasim ibn Ja'far al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Umar al-Lu'lu'i informed us: Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn al-Ash'ath narrated to us: Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Zuhri narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us: Isma'il ibn Umayyah narrated to me, saying: I heard a Bedouin say: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever among you recites *Wa'l-Tin wa'l-Zaytun* and reaches its end, "Is not Allah the most just of judges?" [al-Tin: 8], let him say: 'Yes, and I am among the witnesses to that.' And whoever recites *La uqsimu bi-yawm al-qiyamah* and reaches "Is not that One able to give life to the dead?", let him say: 'Yes.' And whoever recites *Wa'l-Mursalat* and reaches "Then in what statement after this will they believe?", let him say: 'We believe in Allah.'"

[Narrated by Abu Dawud in *al-Salat*, chapter on the measure of bowing and prostration: 1/423; Ahmad: 2/249; al-Hakim authenticated it: 2/510, and al-Dhahabi agreed; al-Bayhaqi in his *Sunan*: 2/310; the author in *Sharh al-Sunnah*: 3/104–105. al-Tirmidhi narrated it in abridged form in *al-Tafsir*: 9/276–277, and said: "This is a hadith that is only narrated with this chain, from this Bedouin, from Abu Hurayrah, and he is not named." al-Suyuti, in *al-Durr al-Manthur*: 8/364, also attributed it to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh. al-Albani, in his commentary on *Mishkat al-Masabih*: 1/272, said: "Its chain is weak, because of Ibn al-A'rabi, who is unnamed."]

Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz informed us: al-Qasim ibn Ja'far informed us: Abu Ali al-Lu'lu'i informed us: Abu Dawud informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Musa ibn Abi A'ishah, who said: A man used to pray on the roof of his house, and whenever he recited "Is not that One able to give life to the dead?" he would say: "Glory be to You, yes!" They asked him about this, and he said: "I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

[Narrated by Abu Dawud in *al-Salat*, chapter on supplication in prayer: 1/422. It is *mursal* (its chain has a gap). Also the author in *Sharh al-Sunnah*: 3/105. See *Awn al-Ma'bud*: 3/139–140.]

**Al-Baghawi's commentary (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on Surah 75, verses 36–40:**

﴿Does man suppose that he will be left neglected (sudan)?﴾ *Sudan* means left aimless, unordered and unforbidden. Al-Suddi said: its meaning is "neglected." It is said of camels: *ibil sudan*, when they graze wherever they wish without a herdsman.

﴿Was he not a drop of semen emitted (yumna)?﴾ That is, poured into the womb. Hafs, from Asim, read *yumna* with a *ya'* (*yumana*). This is also the reading of al-Hasan. The others read it with a *ta'* (*tumna*), referring to the *nutfah* (drop).

﴿Then he became a clinging clot, and He created and proportioned (fasawwa)﴾: He put the spirit into him and perfected his form.

﴿And made of him two sexes, the male and the female﴾: He created from his water offspring, males and females.
